native_mechanisms: Lay the two symbol strings crosswise so their crossings form a lattice of junction points (the pairwise comparison grid).

A single one-cell-wide agent walks the grid in any of eight directions and curls back over its own trail to re-enter a junction from another face (revisiting, label-correcting traversal rather than a fixed sweep).

Each junction stores only a sand mound (its best score so far); a new arrival overwrites a lower mound and discards it, with no separate ledger, and the walk terminates only when no junction can be improved by returning to it.
A sideways crossing that spends nothing, letting one cord slip a step ahead of the other — a zero-cost gap, the single permitted stumble.
core_technique: Standard Needleman-Wunsch global alignment computed as an AVX2 anti-diagonal (wavefront) vectorized DP over three rolling diagonals, with int16/int32 width selection by sequence length and a scalar rolling-row DP fallback.
